subject: Observability & Evals — Discovery notes and action checklist
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@nimbusretail.com>, James Liu <james.liu@skylineai.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -0400
Subject: Observability & Evals — Discovery notes and action checklist

Hi Aisha / James —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written summary so we’re all aligned and have concrete next steps. I tried to keep this focused on the observability + evals scope we discussed.

Key pain points you shared
- Lack of per-route latency breakdowns across model variants; product team cannot correlate regressions to model rollouts.
- No consistent dataset / golden prompt set to measure generation quality changes over time.
- Current tracing is limited to request-level logs (ELK) but lacks token-level KV cache tracing and per-batch metrics.
- Cost drift visibility for high-throughput endpoints; hard to tie cost-per-inference to specific user cohorts.

Current stack (from discovery)
- Frontend: React + Next.js, backend: microservices on GCP (Cloud Run).
- Inference today: managed endpoints (three variants) via self-hosted deployments + a homegrown proxy for routing.
- Observability: ELK stack for app logs, BigQuery for aggregated usage; no LLM-specific dashboards.

Success criteria (how you’ll judge a Redwood proof-of-concept)
1) Able to surface per-route and per-model latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) within the Console dashboards for the routes we pick.
2) Instrumentation that links QA/golden prompts to automated regression alerts (precision drop > X% triggers an alert).
3) Demonstrable tracing hooks or breadcrumbs that map requests to KV cache hits and batch sizes.
4) Clear rollout guardrails: automatic fallback to a lower-cost or smaller model on error rate/latency breach.

Immediate asks you requested
- A sample dashboard layout with the panels above (latency by route/model, cost per token by cohort, regression status for golden prompts).
- Example config for tracing hooks we’d add to your edge proxy (token-level sampling and KV cache annotations).
- A starter golden prompt set (20–30 prompts) relevant to your use cases and a CSV of expected outputs to seed regressions tests.

Deliverables & next steps
- Priya / Redwood: deliver observability_requirements_v1.pdf and golden_prompts_example.csv by EOD Wednesday (attached). Owner: Priya.
- Sergio / Solutions Eng: prepare a short demo (25–30 minutes) showing the Console dashboards for latency & cost, and a run-through of how regression alerts trigger. Proposed slots: Thu 07/22 (10:00–10:30 ET) or Fri 07/23 (11:00–11:30 ET). Owner: Sergio.
- Nimbus: confirm which two routes we want instrumented for the POC and share a sample of your proxy config (or a snippet). Owner: Aisha. Due: Mon 07/26.
- Procurement: James indicated procurement & security review will start around Aug 1. Please share any gating docs we should expect so we can prepare. Owner: James.

Attachments: observability_requirements_v1.pdf (scope + dashboard mockups), golden_prompts_example.csv (starter prompts + expected outputs).

If this looks right, reply with any edits and confirm the demo slot that works best for you.

Thanks —

Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Observability & Evals — Discovery notes and action checklist

Priya —

This is excellent, thank you for the clear summary. A few clarifications from my side:
- Top priority is per-route latency by model variant and the regression alerts tied to our golden prompts; cost dashboards are important but secondary for the POC.
- For the POC routes, please instrument: /checkout/recommendations and /search/autocomplete (these are the two highest-traffic, highest-cost endpoints).
- On the golden prompts: can you include a small customer-facing prompt sample (we’ll need to validate tone and brand voice)? If you can, add a column for acceptable token-range so we can flag length regressions too.
- Procurement timeline: we’ll have legal + infosec engaged; I think James will be the primary contact for procurement questions. We’ll aim to have a short contract out by the first week of August.

Demo slot: Thu 07/22 10:00 ET works for me.

Thanks —
Aisha
Director, Product Analytics | Nimbus Retail
aisha.patel@nimbusretail.com

They want per-route latency by model variant, regression alerts when golden-prompt precision drops beyond threshold, and token-length checks.

Ask list for your demo prep (Thu 07/22 10:00 ET):

- Verify sizing guidance for the two routes (expected qps) so we can recommend batching / quantization profiles in the POC.
